claims.rationale: GATAD2A (p66alpha) acts through a critical coiled-coil interaction with MBD2 to recruit the NuRD corepressor complex for globin gene silencing, supporting that its perturbation will relieve repression of fetal hemoglobin.

EIF2AK1 (HRI) is an erythroid kinase that coordinates translational control and ATF4 activation and modifies beta-thalassemia severity, indicating that perturbing it will alter fetal hemoglobin expression.
ATF4 functions as the central downstream transcriptional effector of the erythroid HRI stress signaling pathway, indicating a key functional role in regulating globin expression.

refusals.reason: Pre-cutoff genetic association in a family pedigree identified ASH1L as an unverified candidate without functional evidence that perturbing it alters fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence lacks functional data showing that perturbing CHD3 regulates fetal hemoglobin expression in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff literature reflects general DNA methyltransferase activity rather than specific functional evidence that selective DNMT1 perturbation regulates fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff records focus on DNMT3A mutations in acute myeloid leukemia and stem cell biology rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff studies associate DNMT3B with lymphomagenesis and general de novo methylation rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
No pre-cutoff evidence demonstrates that perturbing EIF2AK2 regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff literature characterizes PERK in endoplasmic reticulum stress rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation in erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff evidence links GCN2 to general amino acid deprivation responses rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Although eIF2alpha phosphorylation occurs downstream of HRI, pre-cutoff records do not show that specific perturbation of eIF2alpha regulates fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence associates EPAS1 with hypoxia sensing and high-altitude adaptation rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence links FOXO3 to oxidative stress and erythroblast survival rather than direct regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff records provide no functional evidence establishing that perturbing GATAD2B alters fetal hemoglobin.
Functional evidence that inactivating HDAC2 induces gamma-globin expression was already established before the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff literature for HIC2 is restricted to cardiovascular isoform switching without evidence for fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Evidence demonstrating that IGF2BP1 overexpression induces fetal hemoglobin expression in adult erythroblasts was already published before the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence links SETD8 to erythroblast survival and maturation without demonstrating regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
Functional induction of fetal hemoglobin by LIN28B in human erythroblasts was already established prior to the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence implicates TAK1 in inflammatory and necroptotic signaling rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff records do not provide functional evidence that perturbing MAPK1 selectively regulates fetal hemoglobin.
The functional requirement of MBD2 for NuRD-mediated globin gene silencing was already established before the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence indicates MBD3-NuRD does not substitute for MBD2 in mediating globin gene repression.
Pre-cutoff records do not demonstrate that perturbing MTA1 regulates fetal hemoglobin expression.
Pre-cutoff literature lacks functional evidence demonstrating that MTA2 perturbation regulates fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff literature provides no functional data linking MTA3 to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence links NFE2 to adult beta-globin locus activation and heme biosynthesis rather than regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence links NFIX to neural development and progenitor survival without indication of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not establish that perturbing TR2 alone alters fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff studies on TR4 focus on metabolic regulation and macrophage biology rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
No pre-cutoff evidence connects PGRMC1 to erythroid globin switching or fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Although physical binding to BCL11A was described, pre-cutoff evidence does not establish that selective perturbation of this ubiquitous subunit alters fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not provide functional data establishing that perturbing RBBP7 regulates fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff literature does not provide functional evidence that perturbing SMAD1 regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff literature lacks functional evidence establishing SMAD5 as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence associates TET2 with hematologic malignancies and stem cell function rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence focuses on hypoxia response and erythropoietin regulation rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence for Kaiso lacks functional indication of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff records link ZNF143 to promoter architecture and cell cycle without evidence of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
There are no pre-cutoff publications or functional records linking ZNF410 to erythropoiesis or fetal hemoglobin regulation.

notes: 5 of 8 contamination traps passed. These pass by construction under the refusal rule, so a pass shows the time slice held rather than that the system reasoned well. A failure would mean post-cutoff evidence reached the forecast.

Correctly refused and also in the ground truth: ATF4, EIF2AK1, GATAD2A, HIC2, MTA2, NFIX, RBBP4, ZNF410. These count as correct refusals and as missed forecasts at the same time, which is the honest description: the pre-cutoff evidence did not support the claim, and the field found it anyway.
Language-model row. A refusal carries no confidence from the model and is entered at 0 for the calibration error. The cost lens does not apply: the model is not asked for a therapeutic route.
